items.prompt: One arrival pops many monotonic deque candidates. Does that contradict O(n) total actions?

options.text: Yes; every nested while implies quadratic total work
options.why: The total number of pops depends on each index's lifetime.

options.text: No; each candidate is added once and removed at most once
options.why: The amortized total is linear even if one update is expensive.

options.text: No; each update is proven to take identical wall-clock time
options.why: Amortized work does not promise equal latency.

options.text: Yes; a deque can never remove more than one element

items.explanation: Charge each pop to the unique prior push of that index. This bounds the whole sequence, not the worst single arrival latency.
